After playing [[college football]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]], he played as a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] for the [[Houston Oilers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1982 to 1993 and was a nine-time [[Pro Bowl]] selection. Munchak was inducted into the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 2001. After his retirement, Munchak continued his association with the Houston franchise by joining the staff as an offensive assistant in 1994. Munchak was named the offensive quality control coach the following year and stayed with the franchise after it moved to Tennessee and became known as the [[Tennessee Titans]], eventually becoming the offensive line coach in 1997 and serving in that position for 14 years. Munchak became the Titans' head coach in 2011 but was fired after the 2013 season, ending his 31-year association with the franchise. Munchak then served as offensive line coach for the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] from 2014 to 2018 before serving in the same position for the [[Denver Broncos]] from 2019 to 2021. He later served as an offensive consultant for the [[Los Angeles Rams]] in 2023 and 2024.

'''Michael Christopher Minter''' (born January 15, 1974) is an American [[college football]] coach and former player. He is a defensive analyst for [[Western Michigan University]], a position he has held since 2024. He is a former head football coach at [[Campbell University]], a position he held for eleven seasons.<ref>[https://www.si.com/college/fcs/news/campbell-camels-head-coach-mike-minter-resigns-after-11-seasons-fcs-football "Campbell Head Coach Mike Minter Resigns After 11 Seasons"] ''Sports Illustrated''. Retrieved 2023-12-19.</ref> Minter played professionally as a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for ten seasons, from 1997 to 2006, with the [[Carolina Panthers]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska Cornhuskers]] and was selected by the Panthers in the second round of the [[1997 NFL draft]].

'''Michael Elston Phipps''' (born November 19, 1947) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] for 12 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) during the 1970s and 1980s.  Phipps played [[college football]] for the [[Purdue Boilermakers football|Purdue Boilermakers]], and was recognized as an [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]].  He was the third overall pick in the [[1970 NFL draft]], and played professionally for the [[Cleveland Browns]] and [[Chicago Bears]] of the NFL.

He played [[college football]] for the [[Chattanooga Mocs football|Chattanooga Mocs]], winning the [[Jacobs Blocking Trophy]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-knoxville-news-sentinel/164043320/|newspaper=[[The Knoxville News-Sentinel]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=January 18, 1984|page=43|title=Outlaws Get Mike Nease}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mike Nease stats |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/N/NeasMi20.htm |access-date=January 26, 2025 |publisher=Pro Football Reference}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mike Nease, G |url=https://www.nfl.com/players/mike-nease/ |access-date=January 26, 2025 |work=NFL}}</ref> He also played in the [[United States Football League]] (USFL) for the [[Denver Gold]], and had stints in the USFL with the [[Oklahoma Outlaws]] and [[Los Angeles Express (USFL)|Los Angeles Express]] and in the NFL with the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-alexander-city-outlook/164043364/|newspaper=[[The Alexander City Outlook]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=March 6, 1985|agency=[[Associated Press]]|title=Nease hopes protecting Evans is full-time job}} {{Open access}}</ref> He concluded his career with the [[New England Steamrollers]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL) in 1988.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/n/neas00200.html|website=Pro Football Archives|title=Mike Nease Stats}}</ref>
